You are judging SCOPE CONFORMANCE for an already-complete pull request under review — PR #70 in zimmermann-pwa, branch `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection`, HEAD commit 75135712e000ca8957c6a44106b05fe48d2bf61f, base `develop` at 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99. This is a review, not a build step — there is no "plan" document to check against; instead check the diff against the ticket + PRD below. Report a verdict: does this PR deliver exactly SFCC-91's scope, neither under nor over? Do not edit anything.

## The ticket (Jira SFCC-91, verbatim description)

"As a Shopper, I want to see all available colours for a product and be able to switch between them on the page, so that I can explore the full range of colour options before choosing which to buy... This story covers the rendering of colour swatches on the PDP and the interaction logic when a shopper selects a different colour. Swatches are driven by the index image — one product image per colour variation that is designated in SFCC BM as the representative swatch image. Most products do not have a wide range of colours available, however, Dani confirmed max needed number of colours will likely be around 7."

Jira comment history (chronological, all confirmed from the live ticket):
- An AC reading "New Style Code: Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour with a new style code and a full page reload" was explicitly REMOVED from SFCC-91 on 2026-08-12 by the BA (Jasmijn Tsang): "This requires more build - we will cover this AC in SFCC-708." SFCC-708 ("PDP – Related Colours Attribute — BM / frontend") is a separate, still-in-progress story about showing colour swatches from OTHER master products (a different SKU family sharing a colourway) with a full-page navigation between them — confirmed via its TSD (Confluence 458948614, Draft, not yet approved). This is NOT part of SFCC-91's scope. Any code in this PR implementing cross-master-product swatch navigation would be over-scope; the ABSENCE of that feature is correct, not a gap.
- SFCC-91 has issue links: blocked-by SFCC-205 and SFCC-240 (both Figma-to-React spikes, status Done — not blocking), relates-to SFCC-708 (see above, out of scope), relates-to SFCC-737 "pdp/product-content" (in progress — a different developer's concurrent work on the static product header/price block that this PR had to merge/rebase against several times), relates-to SFCC-806 "PDP UI - Colour Swatches & Variation Selection: Development" (status Done — appears to be a dev sub-task tracker, not a scope source of its own).
- Labels: Custom, DesignDependent, PRD-002, PRD-004, Squad-A.

## Relevant PRD (.docs/prd/pdp.md §2 — read the file yourself for full context, this is a summary)

- PRD-002 (confirmed): colour swatches sourced from the Product API (not AP21 — AP21 only carries colour names, not swatch assets).
- PRD-004 (confirmed): "'Also available in' / 'Only available in' colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL." Explicitly states hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour changes on rollover, no click) is "a custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live" — its absence from this PR is correct, not a gap. §18 Open Items also lists "Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC" as still open/TBD — not something this PR needed to resolve.
- PRD-062 (§14, confirmed): "Gallery updates to display variant images when a colour swatch is selected, without a full page reload." This IS in scope for a colour-swatch PR — check whether the implementation actually wires this (client-side URL param update picked up by the base `useDerivedProduct` hook), even if you can't run a browser — read the mechanism and judge plausibility; I am separately verifying this live in a browser myself, so a "can't fully confirm from source" answer scoped to just this one point is acceptable and expected, don't over-claim either way.

## What actually shipped (read the current diff yourself: `git diff 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99 7513571 --stat`, and read the changed files under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`)

A paginated (>4 colours, PAGE_SIZE=4) colour-swatch radiogroup rendered on the PDP only (non-PDP ProductView callers — cart quick-add, wishlist, bonus-product — are unaffected, verified by an optional-prop design where omitting `onColourSelect` preserves the exact pre-existing base SwatchGroup path). Colours with no resolved swatch image or `orderable: false` are fully withheld (not shown disabled) — this was a BA decision confirmed 2026-08-21 per an in-code comment, superseding an earlier "opacity: 0.4 disabled state" reading — treat the BA decision as authoritative over any older design note you might find. A single-colour product shows a text label only, no swatch row. Selecting a colour does a client-side URL update (`history.replace` with `?color=value`), not a full reload. Keyboard arrow navigation with roving tabindex and cross-page hand-off. Translations added for all new user-facing strings. 29 new Vitest tests, Storybook stories, a co-located Chakra recipe.

Also in the diff but check whether it's legitimately load-bearing for SFCC-91 or scope creep: `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (+57/-4) plus a new `scripts/generateRegistry.test.mjs` (81 lines) — a parser-robustness fix to the project's component-registry auto-generation tooling (quote/comment-aware paren-depth tracking so a prop type containing a stray `(` character doesn't corrupt registry extraction). This is unrelated to colour swatches as a *feature* but the PR's own commit messages frame it as necessary because the new component's props broke the existing generator. Judge whether that's a reasonable, minimal, in-scope fix to unblock the PR's own registry regeneration (which `.claude/registry/*.md` changes in this same diff depend on), versus an unrelated drive-by improvement that should have been its own PR.

Also check: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx` gained an `afterContent` prop in an early commit for an approach ("inject colour swatches into the header via a slot") that a LATER commit in the same PR explicitly replaced ("Replace suppressColourAttribute/afterContent approach with colourVariants/selectedColourValue/onColourSelect props on ProductView"). Grep the whole `overrides/` tree for `afterContent` — if nothing outside `staticProductHeader.tsx` and its own test file passes it a real value, that prop (and its dedicated test block) is leftover scaffolding from an abandoned approach that should probably have been removed before merge, not shipped as unused surface area.

Also check translations: `translations/*.json`/compiled counterparts add `colour_swatches.*` keys — confirm these are all actually consumed by the shipped component (no orphaned keys, no missing keys the component references via `intl.formatMessage` that aren't in the catalogue).

Give me: (1) a clear in-scope / under-scope / over-scope verdict per item, (2) specifically call out the `generateRegistry.mjs` change and the `afterContent` leftover as items needing an explicit scope judgment call from me, don't just wave them through, (3) anything else you find that's either missing from SFCC-91's implied scope or present but not asked for.

+/**
+ * Regression tests for generateRegistry.mjs pure-function exports.
+ * Run with: node --test scripts/generateRegistry.test.mjs
+ */
+import { test } from 'node:test'
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
+import { normaliseBody, extractTsProps } from './generateRegistry.mjs'
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// normaliseBody
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+test('normaliseBody: collapses a multi-line function type into one line', () => {
+  const input = [
+    '  validateOrderability?: (',
+    '    variant: SfccVariant,',
+    '    product: SfccProduct,',
+    '  ) => boolean | undefined;',
+    '  showImageGallery?: boolean;',
+  ].join('\n')
+  const result = normaliseBody(input)
+  const lines = result.split('\n')
+  assert.ok(lines.some((l) => l.includes('validateOrderability') && l.includes(') => boolean')),
+    'validateOrderability should be on a single line')
+  assert.ok(lines.some((l) => /^\s{2,}showImageGallery/.test(l)),
+    'showImageGallery should remain its own line')
+})
+
+test("normaliseBody: unbalanced '(' in a line comment does not corrupt depth", () => {
+  // The comment contains a lone '(' with no matching ')' outside quotes.
+  // The old scanner incremented depth for this char, causing the next prop line to be
+  // accumulated into the current one. The fixed scanner stops at '//' and ignores it.
+  const input = [
+    "  onFormat?: (value: string) => string; // e.g. '('",
+    '  label?: string;',
+  ].join('\n')
+  const result = normaliseBody(input)
+  const lines = result.split('\n')
+  assert.ok(lines.some((l) => /^\s{2,}label\?:/.test(l)),
+    "label should be its own line — not absorbed into onFormat's type")
+})
+
+test("normaliseBody: '(' inside a single-quoted string in the type itself is ignored", () => {
+  const input = [
+    "  variant?: 'a(b' | 'c';",
+    '  name?: string;',
+  ].join('\n')
+  const result = normaliseBody(input)
+  const lines = result.split('\n')
+  assert.ok(lines.some((l) => /^\s{2,}name\?:/.test(l)),
+    'name should remain its own line')
+})
+
+test('normaliseBody: characters inside a block comment do not affect depth', () => {
+  const input = [
+    '  /* open paren without close: ( */',
+    '  label?: string;',
+  ].join('\n')
+  const result = normaliseBody(input)
+  const lines = result.split('\n')
+  assert.ok(lines.some((l) => /^\s{2,}label\?:/.test(l)),
+    'label should not be accumulated into the block comment line')
+})
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// extractTsProps — integration: quoted paren in comment
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+test('extractTsProps: retains property after a callback prop whose comment has an unbalanced quoted paren', () => {
+  const content = `
+type TestProps = {
+  onFormat?: (value: string) => string; // e.g. '('
+  label?: string;
+};
+`
+  const props = extractTsProps(content)
+  const names = props.map((p) => p.split(/[?:]/)[0].trim())
+  assert.ok(names.includes('onFormat'), 'onFormat should be extracted')
+  assert.ok(names.includes('label'),
+    "label should be extracted — not swallowed by the comment's quoted paren")
+})

## Scope Conformance Review — PR #70 (SFCC-91)

Base `269d5d4` → HEAD `7513571`, 26 files changed. Read the ticket, `.docs/prd/pdp.md` §2/§14/§18, `CODEOWNERS`, `.claude/rules/{frozenFiles,protectedFiles,squadA,squadB}.md`, the full diff, and traced the PRD-062 mechanism through the base SFCC hooks.

### Hard stop found first, because it changes how to read everything else

`overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` are both modified by this PR's own commit `0fe3c2d` (`feat(design-system): add icon.disabled colour token`), confirmed **not** an ancestor of the `develop` base (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` returned false) — this is new to the PR, not inherited churn:

```diff
 icon: {
   default: grey[900],
+  disabled: grey[200],
 },
```
```diff
 '--zimm-color-icon-default': colors.icon.default,
+'--zimm-color-icon-disabled': colors.icon.disabled,
```

Both paths are explicitly enumerated in `frozenFiles.md`'s Tier 1 Design System list and routed by `CODEOWNERS` to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. AGENTS.md Hard Rule #3 ("Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`") and this reviewer's own instructions ("No Tier 1 file was touched... This is a hard stop") make this unconditional.

Context that matters for your judgment call, not for whether it's a Tier 1 touch (it is, regardless):
- It's real, not orphaned — `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:63` consumes it (`chevronButton['&:disabled'].color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'`) for the pagination chevron's native `disabled` state, which is a distinct concern from AC5's "withhold the whole swatch" decision.
- The commit message cites a Figma node (`40003328:115592–115595`) and states "confirmed by Marcel as Tier 1 approver" — that's a self-attestation inside a commit message, which AGENTS.md's own "Tier 1 Approval" section explicitly says is *not* the enforcement mechanism ("a string in a shared, version-controlled file is not an identity check"). The real gate is the CODEOWNERS-routed review on the actual PR. I have not verified `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members` myself — that's not something a commit message can substitute for.

This is the trigger for the BLOCKED verdict below. I've completed the rest of the scope analysis regardless, since you asked for the full breakdown.

---

### 1. Full manifest against the ticket, with tiers

| File | Tier | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages,utils}.md` | — | Registry churn, expected per your rubric #5, not a finding |
| `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` | **Untiered gap** — see below | In scope (integration point) + 1 trivial drive-by (see §3) |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmColourSwatch.css.ts}` | Tier 3 (ui-kits, both squads) / `.css.ts` → CODEOWNERS squad-only | In scope — the core deliverable |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | Tier 3 (CODEOWNERS: squad-b) | In scope — URL/state wiring |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.{tsx,test.tsx}` | Tier 3 | Partially orphaned — see §2 |
| `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/{default,en,en-GB,en-US,en-XA}.json` | Tier 2 (Translations) | In scope except one stray key, see §3 |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | Tier 2 (UI Designer) | In scope — mechanical recipe registration, required by AGENTS.md's own styling rule |
| `overrides/app/theme/foundation/{colour,zimmTokens}.ts` | **Tier 1** | **BLOCKED — see above** |
| `scripts/generateRegistry.{mjs,test.mjs}` | Untiered | Judgment call — see §2 |
| `translations/{default,en,en-GB,en-US}.json` | Tier 2 | In scope except one stray key, see §3 |

**Aside, not a finding against this PR:** `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` has no entry in `CODEOWNERS` or `protectedFiles.md` at all, despite being consumed by `product-view-modal`, `bundle.jsx`, and `bonus-product-view-modal` in base SFCC — a real governance gap, but pre-existing and not created by this PR.

### 2. The two items you asked me not to wave through

**`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` + `scripts/generateRegistry.test.mjs` — judgment call, leans legitimate.** This isn't a new file inventing new scope; it's a bug fix to an already-existing function (`normaliseBody`, present on `develop` before this PR) that this PR's own `.claude/registry/*.md` regeneration depends on. It's untiered (not in `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`/`CODEOWNERS`), minimal (41 lines in the fixed function, plus a `node:test` regression suite), and comes with a real regression test proving the specific bug (quote/comment-aware paren depth) rather than a speculative hardening pass. I could not find a real trigger for it inside this PR's own new prop comments, though — I checked every new JSDoc block on `ColourVariant`, `ColourSwatchesProps`, and the new `ProductViewProps` fields, and none contain an unbalanced paren inside a comment or string. The commit's own example (`onFormat?: (...) => string; // e.g. '('`) is synthetic, not lifted from a real prop added here. So the fix is real and narrowly scoped, but its necessity for *this specific PR's* registry regen isn't demonstrated by anything in the diff — it reads as "found while regenerating the full registry, fixed in place" rather than "blocked without this." Given it touches no protected path and ships its own test, I'd call this a defensible in-scope inclusion, but it's fair for you to require it as a separate PR on process grounds alone.

**`afterContent` on `staticProductHeader.tsx` — genuinely orphaned, should not have shipped.** Confirmed via repo-wide grep: the only two files referencing `afterContent` anywhere in `overrides/` are `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx` (the prop definition, lines 21-25, and its render, line 111) and its own new test file (`staticProductHeader.test.tsx:81-100`). `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — the only real caller of `StaticProductHeader` — never passes it; the final architecture (commit `4db254b`) routes colour swatches through `ProductView`'s `colourVariants`/`selectedColourValue`/`onColourSelect` props instead. This is dead surface area plus a dead test block from an abandoned approach that a later commit in the same PR superseded but didn't clean up. This is a case for removal before merge, not a hard block.

### 3. Other findings not called out in your prompt

**Stray, unrelated, incompletely-propagated translation key.** `translations/en-GB.json` and `translations/en-US.json` (commit `f9c6c74`, "propagate i18n to en-GB/en-US") both gained `header.button.assistive_msg.search` alongside the five real `colour_swatches.*` keys. That key has nothing to do with SFCC-91 — it's consumed by `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:370` and has existed since the initial commit. Worse, it's a half-fix: `translations/default.json` and `translations/en.json` still don't have it even at HEAD (confirmed via `git show 7513571:translations/default.json | grep`). This is a small, real over-scope touch on a Tier 2 file, unrelated to the ticket, and doesn't even close the gap it appears to be reaching for.

**Trivial drive-by in an already-open file.** `product-view/index.tsx`'s quantity `<label>` moved the colon outside the translated string (`'Quantity:'` → `'Quantity'` + literal `:`) — a CodeRabbit-flagged i18n punctuation fix (per commit `7b7c088`), unrelated to colour swatches, in a file already legitimately open for this PR. Low-risk, same-file, one line — flagging for completeness, not as a real problem.

**E2E coverage was pulled, not silently dropped, but is genuinely absent at merge.** The final commit `7513571` deletes `e2e/features/pdp/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.feature` and its generated spec wholesale, reverting to the `develop` baseline (confirmed clean — no orphaned `.feature`/`.spec` residue anywhere in `e2e/`). The commit message discloses this is deferred to a follow-up pending real fixture SKUs, and the work is stashed locally. This is disclosed, not silent — but it means `testing.md`'s own checklist item ("New user journey → has a `.feature` file") is unmet at the point this PR merges. Worth a conscious decision on your part, not an oversight on mine to paper over.

**Possible unmet pass criterion — "all colours unavailable" case.** `ProductView`'s guard (`product-view/index.tsx`) only checks `!colourVariants?.length` — the *pre*-AC5-filter array. Inside `ZimmColourSwatch` (`index.tsx`), `showSwatches` (line 95) and `labelName` (line 107) are both derived from the *post*-filter `swatchVariants`, but the "Colour:" caption span (lines 189–191) is unconditional inside `labelRow`. So a product whose colour attribute has values, but where every one fails AC5 (no image or non-orderable), renders a bare "Colour:" label with nothing beside it — not "no colour section at all," which is exactly what the now-deleted E2E scenario `A product whose colours are all unavailable shows no colour section at all` specified. This is a static-read finding — I have not run it against real BM data, and it's a narrower case than the common "some colours withheld" path, which works correctly. Worth verifying in your own browser pass.

**PRD-062 mechanism (gallery updates without reload) — plausible, not fully confirmed, as you anticipated.** Traced: `handleColourSelect` (`product-detail/index.tsx`) calls `history.replace` (no navigation) → base `usePDPSearchParams` (`node_modules/.../use-pdp-search-params.js`) reads `useLocation().search` from `react-router-dom`, which re-renders on `history.replace` → `useVariationParams`/`useVariant`/`useDerivedProduct` recompute against the new `?color=` value, the same mechanism the base `<a href="?color=value">` swatch already used. The in-code comment at `product-detail/index.tsx` shows the developer reasoned through exactly this chain rather than inventing a new one. I did not trace the actual gallery-image-selection branch inside `ProductView` itself (unchanged by this diff, so it's pre-existing base wiring) — consistent with your own "can't fully confirm, don't over-claim" framing.

**Confirmed correctly out of scope (no code found, as expected):** no cross-master-product navigation logic (SFCC-708) anywhere in the diff; no hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (PRD-004's explicit exclusion). Both absences are correct, not gaps.

**Confirmed in scope and matching claims:** 29 tests in `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx` (exact grep count), Storybook title `Commerce/ProductView/ColourSwatches` (correctly categorised per `components.md`), all 5 `colour_swatches.*` keys used by the component exist in every source catalogue with no orphans, `filterImageGroups` usage matches the real base SFCC signature (`viewType`/`variationValues`), `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

**Not a finding, just context:** `.claude/rules/squadA.md` (draft) still claims `product-detail/` as Squad A territory while the real, enforced `CODEOWNERS` routes it to `pwa-squad-b` — a pre-existing doc/CODEOWNERS conflict already flagged in `overrideStyling.md`'s "Known gaps," not created by this PR.

---
